stories.title: MALAWI: Caritas Forum Calls for Stronger Solidarity as Disasters Deepen Vulnerability
stories.description:
By Brenard Mwanza
The Caritas Malawi Country Forum 2026 has called for stronger solidarity, coordination and integrity as Malawi faces recurring natural disasters, food insecurity and the growing effects of climate change.
The forum was held in Lilongwe on Thursday, 3 September, bringing together representatives of Caritas organisations, Catholic humanitarian partners and all eight diocesan Caritas offices in Malawi.
Speaking during the meeting, Right Reverend Vincent Frederick Mwakhwawa, Bishop President of the Catholic Secretariat, said the gathering provided an opportunity to assess both the achievements and lessons from humanitarian responses to floods, drought and Cyclone Freddy.
Bishop Mwakhwawa spoke on behalf of Right Reverend Alfred Mateyu Chaima, Bishop President of Caritas Malawi.
He said Caritas Malawi, also known as the Catholic Development Commission in Malawi (CADECOM), was not simply a humanitarian organisation, but part of the Church’s mission to serve people in need.
“Our mission calls us to integrity, compassion, and unwavering commitment to the dignity of every human person,” he said.
Drawing on Catholic Social Teaching and the ministry of charity, the Bishop said the Church must make the Gospel visible through practical service.
“Evangelization is not confined to words; it is also expressed through compassionate presence, solidarity and service,” he said.
Reflecting on Pope Leo XIV’s Apostolic Exhortation Dilexi te, on love for the poor, Bishop Mwakhwawa called for greater attention to people facing multiple forms of vulnerability, particularly women affected by poverty, exclusion, mistreatment and violence.
He urged that Caritas programmes respond to the specific needs of vulnerable groups while strengthening their dignity and resilience.
The forum brought together representatives of Caritas Internationalis, Caritas Africa and Caritas offices from Zambia, Tanzania, Zimbabwe and Eswatini.
International partners included the Scottish Catholic International Aid Fund (SCIAF), Catholic Relief Services (CRS), Trócaire and the Jesuit Centre for Ecology and Development.
Bishop Mwakhwawa thanked partners for financial support, capacity building and solidarity, saying their cooperation had helped Caritas reach thousands of households affected by disasters, food insecurity and climate shocks.
But he warned that stronger partnerships must go hand in hand with accountability.
“We are not like any other organisations; we are faith-based institutions. This identity must define our character,” he said, while calling for greater integrity in the management of resources intended for vulnerable communities.
The forum focused on disaster response, resilience, climate justice, resource mobilisation and closer collaboration within the Caritas family.
On Friday, participants took part in a field visit to Ntchisi District, where they had an opportunity to meet communities benefiting from Caritas programmes.
Bishop Mwakhwawa urged participants to keep those communities at the centre of their work.
“Our strategies, projects and resources ultimately exist for people—for families, women, men and young people whose dignity and hope must remain at the centre of our mission,” he said.
Malawi continues to experience the impact of recurrent floods, droughts and cyclones, with disasters disrupting livelihoods and worsening food insecurity, particularly among already vulnerable communities.
END

stories.title: Probing the thermoelectric properties of the 8-16-4 graphyne monolayer via tight-binding approach
stories.description: In this study, we explore the thermoelectric specifications of the newly proposed 8–16–4 graphyne lattice (GY) by the tight-binding model (TBM) in combination with Green’s function formalism (GFF). The study focuses on how magnetic field, doping, and strain influence key transport parameters, including electrical and thermal conductivity, and Seebeck coefficient. The calculated electronic density of states reveals a Dirac-like semi-metallic behavior, characterized by a vanishing density near the Fermi level. Our results show that applying compressive strain significantly alters the magnitude and position of the conductivity peaks, demonstrating the tunability of transport properties through lattice deformation. The consistently positive value of the Seebeck coefficient throughout the studied temperature window confirms that holes are the primary contributors to thermoelectric transport. However, when viewed as a function of chemical potential, it undergoes a sign change near the neutrality point, signaling a transition between p-type and n-type transport channels. Furthermore, the magnetic field modifies the peak intensity in the electronic states without affecting their position, underscoring the robustness of the band structure. These findings highlight the potential of 8–16–4 GY as a mechanically flexible and thermoelectrically active two-dimensional (2D) material, suitable for applications in nanoelectronic devices and energy conversion technologies.

stories.title: Adaptive Gaussian-weighted nonlinear beamforming with coherence factor enhancement for reflection-mode PLD-based photoacoustic imaging
stories.description: This paper presents a nonlinear beamforming algorithm, the adaptive Filtered Delay Adaptive-Gaussian-Weighted Multiply-and-Sum (F-DaGwMAS), and its coherence factor-augmented variant (F-DaGwMAS + CF), developed to enhance image quality in pulsed laser diode (PLD)-based reflection-mode photoacoustic imaging (PAI). Experimental validation was performed using chicken breast phantoms containing four Indian ink-filled capillary tubes (0.5 mm external diameter) positioned between 4 mm and 22 mm depths. Imaging was conducted at laser pulse energies of 18 µJ, 21 µJ, and 27 µJ. Quantitative analysis showed that F-DaGwMAS consistently outperformed conventional Delay-and-Sum (DAS) and Filtered Delay Multiply-and-Sum (F-DMAS) beamformers across all energy levels. At 27 µJ, F-DaGwMAS achieved 43–67% improvement in spatial resolution relative to DAS and 6–24% improvement compared to F-DMAS. The contrast ratio (CR) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improved by 11–207% and 7–68% over DAS, and by up to 6% and 25% over F-DMAS, respectively. Incorporating coherence factor weighting further enhanced performance, with F-DaGwMAS + CF providing up to 60% better spatial resolution and 1–27% higher CR and SNR than DAS + CF. In addition, in vivo photoacoustic imaging of a healthy human wrist demonstrated clear visualization of cross-sectional view of a vascular structure at depths of approximately 6–8 mm, with improved contrast and reduced noise using the proposed method. These improvements result from the adaptive Gaussian weighting and coherence integration that strengthen coherent components and suppress off-axis noise. The robustness of F-DaGwMAS and F-DaGwMAS + CF across energy levels demonstrates their strong potential for high-contrast, high-resolution PLD-based PAI.

stories.description: Satellite measurements detected declining photosynthetic activity in Western U.S. forests two years before bark-beetle mortality appeared in aerial detection surveys, according to new University of Utah-led research. The first-of-its-kind study suggests that satellite-observed chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), a measure of plant photosynthesis, could provide an early warning of forest stress. As drought, wildfire and insect outbreaks occur with increasing frequency across the American West, the technology could also help scientists understand how these disturbances affect forests’ ability to absorb and store carbon from the atmosphere.
